findings.title: Intermediate CPU rollback above the external-entry baseline remains accepted

contract.requirement: External service-process CPU observations have monotone differences; rollback must refuse, preserving a failed owner.

findings.concrete_trigger: Within the one external phase, let entry CPU be10us, a later check observe20us, and a subsequent check or phase exit observe19us, with wall and charged budget otherwise in bounds. Both20 and19 remain >=externalCpu10, so the rollback is not detected and the estimated CPU charge decreases. The existing CPU rollback test covers only a value below entry baseline (10->9).
findings.analysis: externalCpu is the entry baseline and is never updated by check. It cannot also serve as the last observed monotonic CPU value. cpu() validates type/range only, so intermediate rollback is accepted. No execution or new test was performed by this reviewer.
findings.threat_scope: Clock/observation fault-policy gap in a trusted process.cpuUsage provider. This is not a claim that stock USB input can mutate the clock callback or alter the private pin.
findings.minimal_remediation: Retain the external-entry baseline for cumulative charge while rejecting any CPU sample smaller than the preceding accepted sample; make rollback sticky. findings.title: An observed stream EOF does not immediately invalidate a buffered valid response lease

contract.requirement: EOF invalidates owner/generation before any further eligible output; actual close still forms part of settlement.

findings.concrete_trigger: The peer sends a complete valid response frame and ends the readable stream. If the end event is already observed while that frame is buffered, before the later close event, raw.readLine can still return the frame. The public wrapper has no end listener: it fails only on null read/error or close while !closing. Driver cleanup sets closing=true before raw.close, and completion promotes open->settled. The later close is then deliberately ignored by the lease listener, leaving the generation unchanged and permitting the otherwise valid result.
findings.analysis: SerialLineStreamPort.onEnd marks ended and deliberately drains buffered complete lines; this is reasonable generic transport behavior. It is insufficient to enforce the narrower public fixture EOF revocation contract. connection() checks destroyed only while !closing and therefore does not close this event-ordering window. This is static source/event-order analysis, not a reproduced execution; no test or USB access was performed by this reviewer.
findings.threat_scope: Local Unix stream readable EOF is stock transport input, including relay/USB link termination, not a mutation of trusted callbacks. The finding does not infer remote USB-close attestation from local close, and does not demand such attestation.
findings.minimal_remediation: Invalidate the public fixture on its stream end event before considering buffered frames eligible, e.g. a lease-level end listener. Preserve generic buffered-line behavior. Author can add one focused valid-frame-plus-observed-EOF regression and require refusal/no output without retry.
